title_en: Examples of the Sacrifices of the Shinqiti Scholars
body_ar:
العلماء ورثة الأنبياء، يختارهم الله لحمل دينه وتبليغه للناس، ومن هؤلاء العلماء الذين ضحوا كثيراً وجاهدوا في نشر العلم ورفع علَم الدين علماء الشناقطة، إلا أنهم لم يشتهروا بين الناس، ولم يكن لهم في الدنيا ذكر كثير، بالرغم من شدة عنائهم وتحملهم الظروف القاسية في سبيل العلم منذ القرن الخامس، بل قبله. وقد ذكر الشيخ في هذه المادة نماذج تنبئ عن جهود الشناقطة وتضحياتهم في حفظ العلم وإقامة الدين.
العلماء صفوة الله وورثة الأنبياء:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على نبينا محمد سيد الأولين والآخرين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى أقام الحجة على الناس بالرسل الذين أرسلهم مبشرين ومنذرين ليدلوا الناس على الطريق الذي يرتضي منهم خالقهم سبحانه وتعالى، فما من أمة إلا وفرط فيها رسول دعاها إلى ما يرتضيه منها خالقها سبحانه وتعالى. وعندما ختم الله رسالات الرسل إلى أهل الأرض جعل العلماء ورثة الأنبياء، فجعلهم الحاملين لمشعل الحق والرافعين للوائه، يجاهدون في سبيله ويعلون كلمة الله سبحانه وتعالى بما يبذلون ويضحون، وقد يسرهم الله سبحانه وتعالى لذلك وأعانهم عليه، واختارهم اختياراً من بين خلقه...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* The scholars are the heirs of the prophets, whom God chooses to carry His religion and to convey it to people. Among these scholars who sacrificed much and who strove to spread knowledge and to raise the banner of the religion are the scholars of Shinqit — except that they did not become famous among people, and had no great renown in the world, despite the severity of their hardship and their endurance of harsh conditions for the sake of knowledge from the fifth century onward, and indeed before it. In this material the Sheikh gives examples that tell of the efforts of the Shinqitis and of their sacrifices in preserving knowledge and establishing the religion.

## The scholars are God's chosen and the heirs of the prophets

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, master of the first and the last, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: God, glorified and exalted is He, established the proof against people by the messengers whom He sent as bearers of good news and as warners, to point people to the road with which their Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is pleased. There is no community but that a messenger went before it in it, calling it to what its Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is pleased with from it.

And when God sealed the messages of the messengers to the people of the earth, He made the scholars the heirs of the prophets. He made them the bearers of the torch of truth and those who raise its banner, striving in its path and raising high the word of God, glorified and exalted is He, by what they expend and what they sacrifice. God, glorified and exalted is He, made that easy for them and helped them to it, and chose them — a true choosing — from among His creation …

flags.context: the site's synopsis, dating the Shinqiti scholarly tradition
options: from the fifth century onward — of the Islamic calendar, and so the eleventh century of the common era
from the fifth century of the common era
from the fifth century, era unspecified
flags.note: A date that an English reader will almost certainly misread and that the Arabic leaves unmarked. Arabic historical writing of this kind counts centuries from the Hijra unless it says otherwise, so the fifth century here is the eleventh of the common era; an English reader meeting 'the fifth century' will take it as the fifth of the common era and will be out by six hundred years. The English as written keeps the source's own words and supplies nothing, which is what the style guide requires, but the site must not display this record without resolving the era — either through the Sheikh's office or through a translator's note marked as such.

flags.arabic: فما من أمة إلا وفرط فيها رسول
options: there is no community but that a messenger went before it in it
there is no community but that a messenger was sent among it
read a transcription error for خلا فيها نذير
flags.note: 'فرط' in the sense of going ahead — as a 'فرط' is one who goes before a caravan to the water — gives a reading that works, and that is what the English follows. But the sentence closely echoes Sūrat Fāṭir 35:24, 'وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير', and a transcription slip from that verse is a live possibility. The Sheikh does not present the sentence as a quotation and no citation has been supplied.

flags.context: the opening of the site's synopsis, and again in the Sheikh's transcribed preamble

mark it as a quotation and supply the attribution
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT of the kind noted at records 701 and 705 of this slice. 'The scholars are the heirs of the prophets' is a well-known prophetic report; both the synopsis and the Sheikh's own sentence use it as plain prose, unmarked and unattributed. Reproduced as served in both places; no attribution and no grading has been added.

'الشناقطة' is the plural gentilic of Shinqit, the historic name for the region and its scholarly tradition, from which the Sheikh's own nisba al-Shinqiti derives. The third option has been avoided: 'Mauritania' is a modern state and the tradition described here is older than it, which the synopsis's own dating makes explicit. Proper names are given without diacritics in body text per style guide section 2.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The last record of the Islamic-thought run and, with records 719 and 733's neighbours, one of the few in this slice with a direct bearing on the Sheikh's own tradition: Shinqit is the source of his nisba, al-Shinqiti, and the mahdara tradition described in the style guide's opening section is the subject of this lecture.
The English breaks the transcribed portion into two paragraphs where the source runs on, separating the messengers from the scholars who inherit from them. No word has been added or removed.
The record is the emptiest in the run relative to its title: a lecture announced as giving examples gives none.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record.
